Bringing 3D shoppable products online with generative AI
May 12, 2025
Steve Seitz, Distinguished Scientist, Google Labs
Discover how our latest AI models transform 2D product images into immersive 3D experiences for online shoppers.
Every day, billions of people shop online, hoping to replicate the best parts of in-store shopping. Seeing something that catches your eye, picking it up and inspecting it for yourself can be a key part of how we connect with products. But capturing the intuitive, hands-on nature of the store experience is nuanced and can be challenging to replicate on a screen. We know that technology can help bridge the gap, bringing key details to your fingertips with a quick scroll. But these online tools can be costly and time consuming for businesses to create at scale.
To address this, we developed new generative AI techniques to create high quality and shoppable 3D product visualizations from as few as three product images. Today, we're excited to share the latest advancement, powered by Google’s state-of-the-art video generation model,
Veo
. This technology is already enabling the generation of interactive 3D views for a wide range of product categories on Google Shopping
play silent looping video
pause silent looping video
Examples of 3D product visualizations generated from photos.
First generation: Neural Radiance Fields (NeRFs)
In 2022, researchers from across Google came together to develop technologies to make product visualization more immersive. The initial efforts focused on using
Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF)
to learn a 3D representation of products to render novel views (i.e., novel view synthesis), like 360° spins, from five or more images of the product. This required solving many sub-problems, including selecting the most informative images, removing unwanted backgrounds, predicting 3D priors, estimating camera positions from a sparse set of object-centric images, and optimizing a 3D representation of the product.
That same year, we
announced
this breakthrough and launched the first milestone, interactive 360° visualizations of shoes on Google Search. While this technology was promising, it suffered from noisy input signals (e.g., inaccurate camera poses) and ambiguity from sparse input views. This challenge became apparent when attempting to reconstruct sandals and heels, whose thin structures and more complex geometry was tricky to reconstruct from just a handful of images.
This led us to wonder: could the recent advancements in generative diffusion models help us improve the learned 3D representation?
Our first-generation approach used neural radiance fields (
NeRF
) to render novel views, combining several 3D techniques like
NOCS
for XYZ prediction,
CamP
for camera optimization, and
Zip-NeRF
for state-of-the-art novel view synthesis from a sparse set of views.
Second generation: Scaling with a view-conditioned diffusion prior
In 2023, we introduced a second-generation approach which used a view-conditioned diffusion prior to address the limitations of the first approach. Being
view-conditioned
means that you can give it an image of the top of a shoe and ask the model
“what does the front of this shoe look like?”
In this way, we can use the
view-conditioned diffusion model
to help predict what the shoe looks like from any viewpoint, even if we only have photos of limited viewpoints.
In practice, we employ a variant of
score distillation sampling
(SDS), first proposed in
DreamFusion
. During training, we render the 3D model from a random camera view. We then use the view-conditioned diffusion model and the available posed images to generate a target from the same camera view. Finally, we calculate a score by comparing the rendered image and the generated target. This score directly informs the optimization process, refining the 3D model's parameters and enhancing its quality and realism.
This second-generation approach led to significant scaling advantages enabling us to generate 3D representations for many of the shoes viewed daily on Google Shopping. Today, you can find interactive 360° visualizations for sandals, heels, boots, and other footwear categories when you shop on Google, the majority of which are created by this technology!
The second-generation approach used a view-conditioned diffusion model based on the
TryOn
architecture. The diffusion model acts as a learned prior using score distillation sampling proposed in
DreamFusion
to improve the quality and fidelity of novel views.
Third generation: Generalizing with Veo
Our latest breakthrough builds on
Veo
, Google's state-of-the-art video generation. A key strength of Veo is its ability to generate videos that capture complex interactions between light, material, texture, and geometry. Its powerful diffusion-based architecture and its ability to be finetuned on a variety of multi-modal tasks enable it to excel at novel view synthesis.

• [allears] 以讽刺的语气评论，暗示顶尖人才正在将精力浪费在提升购物体验这样的领域上。
• [ivanjermakov] 质疑是否真的需要用AI来解决3D模型描述格式的问题，认为现有的通用格式已经足够。
• [dm8] 认为该技术是从摄影测量到NeRFs的重大进步，尤其在购物场景中，真实感至关重要，包括光影、纹理和不同环境下的表现。同时对从现有图像/视频中快速创建3D模型的效率表示关注。
• [iamtoomas] 对该技术表示兴趣，但找不到可以试用的链接，表现出对实际应用的渴望。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于该技术是否能在电子商务中提供实际帮助，尤其是在生成3D模型的准确性和效率方面。
- 一些评论者（如[dagmx]和[dm8]）关注技术可能带来的问题，如幻觉、责任和真实性。
- 其他评论者（如[Huxley1]）则看好该技术在特定场景（如小卖家）中的应用潜力。
- [ivanjermakov] 和 [allears] 对该技术是否必要和价值提出质疑，尤其是与现有解决方案的对比。

data.title: Náhuatl and Mayan Language Renaissance Occurring in Mexico
data.author: bryanrasmussen
data.article_summary: 墨西哥拥有68种官方认可的土著语言，近700万人使用，包括玛雅语和纳瓦特尔语。然而，由于城市化、全球化以及西班牙语和英语的主导地位，许多土著语言正面临消亡的威胁。为保护这一丰富的语言遗产，墨西哥政府启动了土著语言课程和双语课程的计划。在尤卡坦州，约35,000名学生可以选择学习尤卡坦玛雅语。墨西哥城将有78所学校开设纳瓦特尔语课程。尽管资源有限和方言差异等挑战依然存在，学生和社区的热情日益增长，显示出土著语言在墨西哥身份认同中的持久价值。同时，土著语言还面临着历史遗留的歧视问题，保护这些语言不仅是保存词汇，更是维护土著人民的尊严和身份。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕墨西哥土著语言（特别是纳瓦特尔语）的复兴、重要性及其实际可行性的讨论

不同观点：
• [jf的观点] 认为纳瓦特尔语在墨西哥的复兴可能与墨西哥的“印第根主义运动”有关，并对纳瓦特尔语在墨西哥西班牙语及全球语言中的影响感到着迷。个人家族历史也激发了其对这一语言的兴趣。
• [dhosek的观点] 指出“玛雅语言”这一术语具有误导性，因为玛雅文化包含多种语言，而不仅仅是单一的语言。同时强调了墨西哥是世界上语言最多样化的国家之一，但人们往往将原住民文化扁平化，误认为某些文化已经灭绝。
• [eschulz的观点] 分享了个人经历，指出在墨西哥仍有许多年轻人讲土著语言（如萨波特克语），强调了土著语言在现代墨西哥社会中的实际存在。
• [ogogmad的观点] 提出是否有可能复兴玛雅象形文字，即便是在有限的形式下。
• [neilshev的观点] 对濒危语言的复兴持悲观态度，指出尽管有努力恢复（如爱尔兰的盖尔语），但成效不佳。认为在全球化背景下，本土语言容易被视为“无用”或“古老”，复兴非常困难，除非采取强制措施。
• [stackedinserter的观点] 持现实主义态度，认为在全球主流语言（如英语、西班牙语）的强大吸引力下，土著语言很难复兴。除非社会结构发生变化（如回到村落生活），否则趋势难以逆转。
• [thunder-blue-3的观点] 认为墨西哥有更紧迫的问题（如暴力和基本人权问题）需要关注，不应优先考虑语言复兴问题。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了纳瓦特尔语、萨波特克语和玛雅语言等多种墨西哥土著语言，显示了语言多样性的复杂性。
• 评论中还提到了不同的个人经历和观察，例如[eschulz]提到的在墨西哥城的土著语言使用者，以及[dhosek]在Chiapas和危地马拉的经历，这些都为讨论提供了现实背景。
• 争议的焦点在于复兴土著语言的优先级和可行性，一些评论者认为有更紧迫的社会问题需要解决，而另一些评论者则对复兴这些语言的努力持怀疑态度，认为在全球化背景下成功的机会很小。

43974461.article_content:
Mexico is home to 68 officially recognized Indigenous languages, spoken by nearly 7 million people, including Mayan and Náhuatl. Yet, despite their historical significance, many of these languages are in decline. Urbanization, globalization, and the dominance of Spanish and English are slowly but surely pushing them to the brink.
To preserve Mexico’s rich linguistic heritage, Mexican authorities have kick-started an initiative to offer Indigenous language classes, and, in some cases, fully bilingual curriculums.
In Yucatán, efforts to teach the Maya language in schools are gaining momentum as 35,000 students from 75 municipalities now
have the option to study Yucatec-Maya
, beginning as early as grade school.
Náhuatl and Mayan Language Renaissance
The broader initiative includes efforts to preserve and revitalize Indigenous culture by recognizing the importance of Mexico’s Prehispanic heritage and how it connects with its cultural and historical significance.
The Mexican government’s commitment to this cause is reflected in the General Law of Linguistic Rights of Indigenous Peoples, which recognizes Indigenous languages as having equal validity with Spanish.
In Mexico City,
78 schools
will begin offering Náhuatl language classes in the next few weeks. Although Náhuatl is the most widely spoken Indigenous language on the entire American continent, it shows signs of quickly vanishing, especially among younger generations.
Classical age Maya stelae of Yaxilan depict two nobles in conversation. Photo: Carlos Rosado van der Gracht / Yucatán Magazine
“Náhuatl has since time immemorial been the language of the people of the valley of Mexico, but it’s not just a tongue of the past. It must be preserved as a living language into the future as part of our nation’s heritage,” said Mexico City Mayor Clara Brugada.
Across the country, similar initiatives are underway to promote the use of Indigenous languages like Zapotec and Mixtec, which have been spoken for centuries but now face the threat of extinction.
These classes are designed to teach vocabulary and grammar and immerse students in the cultural context of the languages. Through storytelling, traditional songs, and rituals, students gain a deeper understanding of the worldviews embedded in these ancient tongues.
In Yucatán, adult students can enroll in
Mayan language
classes at
INDEMAYA
, the Autonomous University of Yucatán, the Municipal Mayan Language Academy “Itzamná,” as well as at the UNAM’s
Cephcis language center
.
Growing Enthusiasm  for Indigenous languages
While challenges such as limited resources and varying dialects persist, the growing enthusiasm among students and communities signals a promising future for Indigenous languages, ensuring they remain an enduring part of Mexico’s identity.
It is important to keep in mind that indigenous languages in Mexico, are often met with discrimination. This prejudice stems from a complex web of historical, social, and economic factors that continue to marginalize indigenous communities.
The roots of this discrimination trace back to the Spanish colonization of Mexico. Spanish colonizers imposed their language and culture, creating a hierarchy where indigenous languages were deemed inferior. This legacy of cultural erasure persists today, as Spanish remains the dominant language in education, media, and government, while indigenous languages are often excluded from these spaces.
Social and racial prejudices further compound the issue. Indigenous people, who are frequently among the poorest in Mexico, face stereotypes that label their languages and cultures as “backward” or “outdated.” Speaking an indigenous language can lead to discrimination in urban areas, where Spanish is seen as the language of opportunity and modernity.
The fight for indigenous languages in Mexico is not just about preserving words; it’s about reclaiming identity, dignity, and a place in a society that has long marginalized its native peoples. By embracing linguistic diversity, Mexico can move closer to a future where all its voices are heard and valued.
Carlos Rosado van der Gracht
Senior Editor Carlos Rosado van der Gracht is a Mexican expedition/Canadian photographer, adventure leader, and PhD candidate. Born in Mérida, Carlos holds multimedia, philosophy, and translation degrees from universities in Mexico, Canada and Norway.

data.title: Comma 3X: Initial Impressions
data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Comma 3X设备的功能、合法性、安全性及其在驾驶中的应用，特别是对于有健康问题（如眩晕症）的驾驶者的适用性。

不同观点：
• Vasco和Havoc认为，让有严重眩晕症的人驾驶车辆是危险的，尤其是在紧急情况下无法保证控制车辆，这可能危及他人安全。Vasco提到不同地区对驾驶健康条件的法规不同，而Havoc则认为这种做法简直疯狂。
• Mscbuck对Comma 3X持积极态度，认为其在交通和高速驾驶中表现良好，尤其是在与原车系统对比时，驾驶体验更好，但他也提到新模型在训练架构上的改进不如预期。
• Shellfishgene对在美国可以安装此类开源硬件和软件以控制车辆转向和刹车表示惊讶，因为在其他地方，安装未经认证的汽车部件可能不合法。
• Edude03对开源项目的收费问题提出质疑，认为开放源代码并不等同于免费，且开发需要成本，因此对每月收费感到不满的人表示不理解。
• Theparanoid分享了个人使用Comma 3X的经验，认为其在高速公路驾驶中表现良好，但不适合城市街道。
• Nancyminusone对Comma Prime的广告过多表示不满，并对产品公开声称的某些功能表示怀疑，特别是关于眩晕症驾驶者的使用。
• Mtlynch表示对AI驾驶控制持怀疑态度，但希望有系统能提供驾驶安全反馈，帮助避免危险情况。
• Optimusprinceps和Krosaen则对Comma 3X的具体功能和法律责任问题表示困惑和担忧，尤其是产品使用中的责任归属和潜在风险。
• Farmdve对Comma设备的概念感兴趣，但对其安装和修改车辆固件的要求感到不安，尤其是涉及安全系统如ABS时。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于Comma 3X设备的合法性、安全性及其对驾驶者（特别是健康状况特殊的驾驶者）的适用性。
• 不同用户对开源项目的收费和责任归属问题存在分歧。
• 实际使用经验分享显示出对产品功能和可靠性的不同看法，尤其是在高速和城市驾驶中的表现。
• 对AI驾驶辅助技术的信任问题和潜在法律责任是用户关注的重点。

data.title: "Goodwill", key member of the SoCal Python Community has passed away
data.author: rdegges
data.article_summary: 本文是悼念Southern California Python社区的组织者Michael Ryabushkin（网名goodwill）的悼文。他于2025年5月初去世，对社区的影响深远。Michael多年来组织了多次活动和会议，如SoCal Python和PyBeach，还为多个开源项目和社区做出贡献。他以无私的帮助和善意著称，总是乐于介绍人们互相认识，创造职业机会和友谊。他鼓励他人回馈社区，并以导师和朋友的身份支持许多人，包括帮助别人转行技术领域。他的幽默、善良和无私让很多人怀念。Michael的离去是社区的重大损失，他将被深深怀念。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对Michael的缅怀与赞扬，以及他在Python开发者社区中的贡献

不同观点：
• [rdegges] 对是否发布纪念消息存在犹豫，但最终决定分享。他强调Michael是一个善良的人，对洛杉矶Python开发者社区的成长贡献卓著。他还提到Michael是一个优秀的工程师和黑客，并邀请认识Michael的人在他的纪念页面上分享经历。

• [cafard] 简单直接地表达了对Michael的赞赏，称他为一个杰出的人，但没有提供具体细节。

• [john-tells-all] 详细描述了Michael对社区的无私奉献，包括他如何不知疲倦地帮助人们建立联系，确保大家都能享受社区活动。他还提到Michael积极寻找并鼓励像他这样的演讲者和教师。John表示很乐意通过讲述Michael的故事来缅怀他。

补充讨论：
• Michael的个人品质和对社区的贡献是大家讨论的重点，特别是他帮助连接社区成员和鼓励新人参与的活动。
• 不同的评论者通过各自的视角分享了对Michael的回忆和感激，展现了Michael的多方面影响。
• 争议方面，评论中没有明显的对立观点或争议，所有评论者都一致对Michael表达了高度的赞扬和怀念。

44001734.article_content:
In Memoriam: Michael
In early May of 2025, the long-standing SoCal Python organizer Michael Ryabushkin—known to many as goodwill—passed away.
As possibly the person most responsible for years of thriving of the group and its surrounding community, he had an impact on many of us, both professionally and personally. In light of that, this page is a collection of
in memoriam
messages submitted through
this form
. If you would like to share your memories of Michael, please do the same.
Michael and I met in 2017, when I started attending SoCal Python meetups. Pretty soon he brought me under his wing as a co-organizer, and over the ensuing years we and others organized many SoCal Python events together, and even the inaugural PyBeach conference. His helpfulness and influence on everything he contributed to are hard to overstate. He was engaged in many other communities as well, and it’s no secret or surprise that many people active in them knew him and appreciated his work.
Somewhere in there Michael and I became friends as well. I don’t know if he knew how to operate in any other way, and I think that line was rather blurred for him in general, since he always sought ways to help other people. The number of times I’ve witnessed him introduce two people to each other is beyond any count, and that’s basically what he was about: making connections. These connections lead to job opportunities, friendships, and who knows what else.
The Southern California Python community has lost one of its major champions, and he will be greatly missed. Rest in peace, goodwill.
— Nik Kantar, May 2025
I met Michael at a PyLadies event in 2011.  He'd offered his company's office space for some of the workshops and hackathons that PyLadies was running at the time. That was the first of many events that we would organize together, over more than a decade. When SoCal Python needed more organizers in 2013, Michael volunteered countless hours to organize monthly meetups where folks from LA and Orange Counties could gather to share knowledge, stories, and skills with each other. On top of that, Michael wrangled his employer into sponsoring numerous events and open source projects, including Plone and Pyramid, Nix, PyCon US, the SoCal Linux Expo, and so many more.  His work helped sustain an active commmunity of hundreds of Python and open source enthusiasts.
Michael always kept a keen eye out for those in need of help. He would never hesitate to give generously of his time and resources.  Michael once told me "a stranger is just a friend you haven't met yet", and he had many friends, whether they knew it or not!  At the time I met Michael, I was freelancing part-time as a web developer to make ends meet. Michael convinced me to change careers, assuring me against my many doubts that I could be successful as a full-time software developer, even opening up a junior developer role at his company to hire me into my first professional job in tech. Without exaggeration, Michael forever changed the course of my life, as he changed the lives of many others.
Michael loved terrible jokes and puns, often repeating his favorites to the point where everyone got sick of them (I suspect this had to be one more reason why he loved meeting new people, for whom these jokes would be fresh material again!). At tech conferences, he made his presence known almost everywhere, as he sought out new people to get to know better, and talked with old friends and new, sometimes through the night - sleep was an after-thought during such weeks.
The SoCal Python community will not be the same without Michael. He was a true leader, a great mentor, and a friend without peer. I will miss him terribly.
— Esther, May 2025
For a few years, Michael was my manager. For many more years, he was also my mentor and friend. He saw his purpose in challenging people and breaking them out of their boxes. He loved to teach, and was always generous with his time. And he encouraged me to give back by helping, advising, and mentoring others. I can't believe Michael is not with us anymore. But I'm not going to forget his passion, humor, and kindness.
— Irina T, May 2025
I met Michael in 2016, and from the very beginning, it was clear why so many people were drawn to him. He had a rare and disarming kindness—one that didn’t hesitate, didn’t judge, and never asked for anything in return. Michael gave freely: his time, his energy, his resources, and most of all, his heart. He lived up to the name many knew him by—Goodwill—not just in spirit but in practice, every single day.
When I was going through one of the darkest chapters of my life, it was Michael who reached out. We weren’t close then—barely even friends—but that didn’t matter to him. He offered support without hesitation, helped me find my footing when I couldn’t stand on my own, and reminded me that I wasn’t alone. data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：OpenAI 收购 WindSurf 及其对编码专用 AI 模型的影响

不同观点：
• **resters 的观点**：
   - OpenAI 收购 WindSurf 是基于对其模型的尽职调查和潜在价值的评估。
   - WindSurf 可能通过用户数据帮助训练编码专用 AI 模型，从而为 OpenAI 带来六个月的领先优势，这可能值 30 亿美元。
   - 即使 WindSurf 的模型在编码方面并非最优，但在某些关键领域的卓越表现足以证明对其方法论的大量投资是合理的。
   - 当前的顶级模型在处理特定框架、编程语言版本等方面仍有改进空间，尤其是在支持较 obscure 的语言和库版本方面。

• **antirez 的观点**：
   - 收购可能导致用户被迫使用较弱的模型，而不是最好的可用模型。
   - "AI inside the editor" 模式限制了开发者的自由，使设计交互过于关注代码而非设计本身。
   - 不能同时订阅多个顶级 LLM 并根据需要选择使用，这降低了灵活性。

• **bluelightning2k 的观点**：
   - ** cynical 看法**：将自己描述为全栈 AI IDE 公司听起来很有投资吸引力，可能要求更高的估值。
   - ** optimistic 看法**：针对特定用例（不完整代码片段和特定数据模型）进行微调应是有效的，具备合理的技能和经验。
   - ** bonus 看法**：可能意味着他们正在通过大规模收集用户数据进行训练。

• **firejake308 的观点**：
   - 困惑于 WindSurf 为什么在即将被 OpenAI 收购的情况下还要开发自己的前沿模型，可能是在收购前已经进行的工作。

• **blixt 的观点**：
   - WindSurf 的编辑器提供了有价值的洞察，帮助构建新的数据模型和训练方法，这对于创建全自动软件工程师非常有价值。
   - 相比之下，其他基础模型提供商可能只能依赖二手数据进行长周期工程工作的模拟。

• **dyl000 的观点**：
   - OpenAI 拥有大量优质数据，训练自己的模型是必然的，且 Claude API 调用可能影响其盈利能力。
   - 提到一个开源替代方案，但指出该方案存在问题。

• **aquir 的观点**：
   - 由于开发工作需要特定的 VSCode 扩展，只能选择 VSCode+Copilot 或 Cursor，限制了选择。

• **infecto 的观点**：
   - 请求提供 arm Linux 版本的构建。

补充讨论：
- 讨论中涉及模型训练数据的获取、处理和价值，尤其是用户数据的重要性。
- 不同用户对使用特定编辑器扩展的依赖性和选择受限的问题。
- 对开源替代方案的提及和对不同平台支持的需求（如 arm Linux 构建）。
- 争议的焦点在于收购后的模型选择和用户体验的自由度，以及开源与专有解决方案的对比。

data.author: wyxuan
data.article_summary: 《The Browser Company》推出了新浏览器Dia，旨在通过AI功能超越Chrome。Dia源于公司对Arc浏览器的经验，后者在2021年推出，但去年进入了维护模式。Dia的特点包括一个智能URL栏和内置的GPT 4.1聊天界面，可以根据查询内容自动路由至聊天模式。虽然Dia在某些方面表现不错，如内置广告拦截器优于uBlock Origin Lite，但也存在一些问题，如侧边栏占用过多屏幕空间，影响网站显示。此外，Dia在创新功能上尚未显现出独特的“惊艳”效果，而Google在AI能力上可能更具优势。文章认为Dia若要成功，需在创新功能上表现出色，否则可能重蹈Arc的覆辙，但也存在因Google面临反垄断问题而获得优势的可能性。

Home
Blog
Dia Review
Dia – an early review
Published
May 11, 2025
⋅
Updated
May 13, 2025
⋅
3
minutes
read
The Browser Company of New York (BCNY), known for
Arc
, has just launched Dia through their alpha program – their latest take on the web browser.
Just as some background, BCNY created Arc in 2021, but late last year they put Arc on maintenance mode.
At the core of this decision was that even though Arc had great traction, they needed something that would put it solidly ahead of Chrome – having a better UI wasn't enough to create a long term business.
They decided to make an AI native browser – the result of which is Dia.
As an early Arc adopter and daily user, I was keen to take it for a spin.
This is a picture of what the UI looks like:
You have a sidebar on the right which can be triggered via
cmd
+
shift
+
e
, and the default new tab view is a search engine box that doubles as a chat interface.
The base model that you chat with is GPT 4.1, and the inline chat has the current page's content as context.
Features
Dia introduces several interesting ideas:
The URL bar is neat: it pulls the query string for searches or displays the URL base and page title, rather than the full link.
It intelligently routes queries. For example, if your query is phrased as a question (i.e. it begins with where, what, who, etc.), Dia routes it directly to its chat interface.
This is a smart move, as making chat the default for all searches (an issue I've found with trying to set Perplexity as a default search engine) would introduce unwelcome latency for basic searches.
It's got some small issues though:
if you search 'werewolves', it still thinks it's a chat query.
if you paste in a link, weirdly it tries to search it up instead of navigating to the site directly.
The ability to toggle between the two modes is clever.
Issues
The spacing of the screen is a big issue:
Fullsize on a display (Macbook Pro) - the sidebar for Arc is roughly 1/5 of the screen.
While the AI chat sidebar takes up 3/10 of the screen real estate.
This really hurts usability for websites, as it creates an awkward dimension that many sites don't support well, leading to content reflow or truncation.
Arc's sidebar doesn't play well with some sites to begin with, and having a sidebar almost double the size doesn't help.
It's not Dia's fault, and you aren't always chatting with websites, but if this is a unique selling point for Dia, it better work well.
That said, the built-in adblocker is quite good – even better than uBlock Origin Lite.
On
https://adblock.turtlecute.org/
Dia gets 77%, while uBlock Origin Lite gets 70%.
Conclusion
If BCNY's stated goal for Dia was to create a browser similar to Chrome for an easy switch, they've clearly succeeded – the resemblance is striking. The rationale makes sense. However, it's a tricky position. For the features where Dia aims to innovate and differ from Chrome, they
really
need to stand out. In other words, if you come for the king, you better not miss.
I think Google has stronger AI competencies and is better positioned to execute on these different agentic features. Consider a feature like agentic browsing: this requires multimodal capabilities that are not widely available and an infrastructure that can serve these AI features affordably enough to billions of users.
Personally speaking, Dia is missing the 'wow' factor I felt with Arc when I first used it—like its novel sidebar interactions and profile switching. I suspect those accustomed to quick profile switching in Arc will sorely miss it in Dia.
Some possible directions I can see this going:
The bear case:
BCNY gives up on building Dia and instead figures out how to continue with Arc – this I feel is the most likely outcome.
The bull case:
Google faces antitrust issues and/or is unable to execute as well on their AI-integrated browser, giving a significant advantage to Dia while they refine their offering.
Dia finds a way to make users truly love the product (perhaps through exceptional agentic features or a standout design?).
In any case, I will always respect those willing to push all the casino chips in. BCNY is clearly doing that with Dia, and if they succeed, it will be a magical product.

• [Dia的评价和期待]
  - **mdrzn**：对Arc不感兴趣，但对Dia有期待，希望有机会试用。
  - **teo_zero**：幽默地提到Dia在处理搜索查询时的一些 quirks。
  - **skarat**：认为Arc有一些 quirks 使其不能作为日常浏览器使用，Dia可能只是一个功能的延伸。

• [商业模式与市场策略]
  - **danpalmer**：深入分析了BCNY在Arc上的商业模式问题，认为他们未能找到可持续的盈利方式，并过多依赖VC资金，试图成为大企业，而不是专注于小而稳定的收入模式。
  - **gnabgib**：提供了一个相关链接，讨论BCNY正在开发第二个更简单的浏览器，暗示公司可能在尝试不同的产品策略。

补充讨论：
• **其他工具的提及**
  - **ipsum2**：提到另一个名为Dia的开源TTS模型，并提供其GitHub链接。

争议焦点：
• **技术基础选择**：选择Blink/Chromium还是Webkit作为浏览器基础。
• **Arc的终止和Dia的推出**：对Arc停止开发的原因和转向Dia的合理性存在不同看法。
• **商业模式**：BCNY在Arc上的商业模式失败原因以及Dia未来可能的发展方向。

这些观点共同描绘了技术社区对浏览器技术选择、产品发展以及商业模式的关注和思考。

data.title: Meta Battles an 'Epidemic of Scams' as Criminals Flood Instagram and Facebook
data.author: erehweb
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Facebook及其母公司Meta在处理用户生成内容和付费广告中存在的问题，尤其是在诈骗和虚假广告方面的不足。

不同观点：
• [plantain] 认为Facebook上的付费广告缺乏审查，甚至出现药物和假币广告，且没有任何人工或先进的LLM（大语言模型）进行把关。这让人质疑Facebook在处理付费广告时的责任心。
• [sanswork] 指出Facebook在处理诈骗和垃圾信息时反应迟钝，即使是低级的诈骗手段也未能有效阻止，举报后常常得到“未违反规则”的反馈，显示出平台在处理这些问题上的不作为。
• [RajT88] 分享了自己合法使用Facebook广告却遭遇支付问题导致先前广告活动被重新启用的经历，认为大科技公司在处理可能影响其收入的漏洞时反应迟缓，可能需要外部压力（如国会传唤）才能解决。
• [bluecalm] 举报了一个明显的诈骗页面，但Facebook的举报系统无法准确传达问题，且公司未认真核查公司是否存在。这表明Facebook在防止非法活动方面的漠视。
• [ggm] 提到Meta因未阻止使用高净值人士身份进行金融科技诈骗的广告而面临法律诉讼，显示问题的严重性。
• [edarchis] 和 [42lux] 都认为Facebook从诈骗活动中获利，而不是积极阻止。他们举报了明显的诈骗广告，但收到的反馈是“未违反社区标准”。
• [conartist6] 和 [jazzcomputer] 分享了个人经历，指出即使举报了假冒账户，Facebook往往也不会采取有效行动，这导致诈骗账户长期存在。
• [hn_throwaway_99] 引用了有关“杀猪盘”诈骗集团的报告，认为Meta的不作为助长了这种犯罪活动，并认为Meta为了利益而无视这些问题，对社会造成了负面影响。
• [jaoane] 提到在Facebook上看到的加密货币诈骗广告，使用AI生成的政治人物视频进行欺骗，且这些广告来自第三世界国家，质疑Facebook的广告地域定向问题。

补充讨论：
• [stevenicr] 提到在TikTok上也出现了类似的假冒身份诈骗，导致一些用户被骗钱。这显示出社交媒体平台普遍面临诈骗问题，可能影响用户对数字平台的信任。
• [liendolucas] 对Meta声称的努力持怀疑态度，认为其并不关心问题的解决。

争议焦点：Facebook和Meta在处理用户生成内容和付费广告中的审查不力，尤其是在诈骗和虚假广告方面的漠视，用户对其不作为感到不满。

data.title: Huawei is spamming open source community for its Harmony ecosystem (See Comment)
data.author: fernvenue
data.article_summary: 这篇文章总结了多个针对OpenHarmony系统进行的适配提案，涉及多个开源项目，如pako、ThreadPool、snappyjs、brotli、libgphoto2、stlport、hi-base32、CaverPhone和EventBus等。每个提案都简要介绍了项目背景，说明了OpenHarmony作为广泛应用于智能终端的开源操作系统，适配这些项目的必要性。提案中还提到了一些具体的适配工作内容，如提供演示和遵循OHPM规范等。这些提案由不同用户提交，提交时间各异，大多数仍在开放状态。文章还提示了如何利用GitHub Issues来规划和跟踪工作。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对OpenHarmony项目及其相关代码提交质量的评价与争议

不同观点：
• Disposal8433认为OpenHarmony项目中的问题描述和代码提交质量低下，具体表现为无解释的代码提交和无意义的代码重复，并借此批评华为公司。
• fernvenue关注链接问题，试图提供一个相关链接，但未直接参与对代码质量的讨论。
• garylkz持中立态度，指出开发者有自由提交提案，但也提到即使提案被拒绝，提交者可能会选择复制项目并自行修改，暗示这种做法可能不够理想。
• rhzdgaf以讽刺和质疑的语气提出对OpenHarmony的负面看法，将其与阴谋论联系在一起，显示出对该项目的强烈不信任。
• stop50支持Disposal8433的观点，进一步批评项目中的代码重复问题和存在无用文件。
• pogue对OpenHarmony的实际可用性表示疑问，询问是否可以在个人设备上安装和试用。
• aitchnyu对OpenHarmony项目中适配JavaScript库的行为表示不解，认为在没有假设恶意或无能的前提下，这种做法的必要性不明确。

补充讨论：
• 评论中对OpenHarmony项目的技术质量和动机存在明显争议，部分评论者如Disposal8433和stop50对代码质量提出具体批评，而rhzdgaf则从更广泛的政治和安全角度进行质疑。
• garylkz的观点提供了一种平衡，既承认开发者的自由，也指出了可能的不良开发实践。
• aitchnyu的疑问则涉及项目技术需求的合理性，试图从技术角度探讨该项目某些做法的必要性。

争议焦点：OpenHarmony项目的代码质量及其动机和安全性受到质疑，尤其是代码提交和适配工作的合理性和技术水平成为讨论的核心。

data.title: Orcas abandoned in shuttered marine park filmed in algae-infested pool
data.author: rguiscard
data.article_summary: 法国马林兰公园关闭后，园内最后两只虎鲸被困在充满藻类的池中，健康和安全受到严重威胁。动物权益组织呼吁法国政府尽快将它们转移到其他保护设施，但相关转移计划屡遭拒绝，包括日本和西班牙的海洋公园。虎鲸Wikie和其11岁的儿子Keijo因在人工环境中出生，无法被放归野外。目前，救援团队正努力将它们安置到加拿大新斯科舍省的一个保护区，但时间紧迫，情况危急。同时，园内还有12只海豚同样被困。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对文章内容简短和信息不足的质疑，以及对欧盟和动物福利的关注。

不同观点：
• Junon认为文章过于简短，质疑其真实性。他们指出文章仅有三个段落和一张照片，无法全面说明事件的背景和细节，尤其是关于为何动物被遗弃在公园以及相关责任人的考量。
• Junon对欧盟可能涉及此事件表示怀疑，认为欧盟不会故意允许这种动物福利问题发生。他们对于事件背后的原因表示关注，尤其是公园发生了什么，以及为什么没有采取措施保护动物。

补充讨论：
• Junon的评论反映了对信息透明度和细节的需求，尤其是涉及到公共利益和动物福利的问题时，读者希望获得更深入的报道和解释。
• 评论中还隐含了对相关责任方的质疑和批评，认为在处理动物福利问题上应有更多的关注和行动。

44001632.article_content:
Breaking News

France’s last two captive orcas were filmed stranded in an algae-infested marine park near Cannes months after the park closed, leaving the fate of the marine mammals uncertain.
Animal activists have circulated footage of the killer whales’ plight in the hopes that the French government will rehome them before it’s too late.
“The orcas need to be removed from dangerous conditions that are posing significant risks to their health and safety,” pleaded Marketa Schusterova, co-founder of the animal advocacy group TideBreakers, which shared the heartbreaking video, South West News Service reported.
4
Drone footage shows Wikie and Keijo trapped in Marineland.
TideBreakers / SWNS
Marineland Antibes reportedly shuttered on Jan. 5, in line with France’s bans on dolphin and whale shows enacted in 2021, leaving the two orcas, Wikie, 23, and her 11-year-old son, Keijo, trapped inside their pens along with 12 dolphins.
Heartrending aerial footage shows the cetaceans languishing in algae-choked pools in a derelict stadium, like a scene out of a post-apocalyptic SeaWorld.
Explore More
Noah’s Ark site’s ‘fully preserved’ secrets discovered in radar scans: ‘Not what you’d expect to see’
Once considered impossible –Physicists turned lead into gold
Huge solar storm to blame for colossal global blackouts — and there are more to come, experts say
“The situation in Marineland Antibes is an emergency and needs worldwide attention,” lamented Schusterova. “These are the last two remaining orcas in captivity in France and they should be moved quickly.”
4
Managers at Marineland (pictured), which is still legally responsible for the animals until they can be rehomed, stressed that Wikie and Keijo “must leave now” for their own welfare.
Anadolu via Getty Images
Unfortunately, campaigns to rehouse the majestic beasts have so far fallen flat with French authorities, who are blocking efforts to transfer the animals to a marine zoo in Japan.
Meanwhile, Spanish authorities rejected a proposal to move the animals to Loro Parque marine park in Tenerife, claiming that the facility — which is already home to four orcas — did not have enough space to “house the specimens in optimal conditions,”
BBC reported.
4
“The orcas need to be removed from dangerous conditions that are posing significant risks to their health and safety,” pleaded Marketa Schusterova, co-founder of the animal advocacy group TideBreakers, which shared the heartbreaking video.
TideBreakers / SWNS
Lori Marino, president of the Whale Sanctuary Project, is currently campaigning to have Wikie and Keijo rehomed to their site in Nova Scotia, Canada, which she feels could be the “only option left.”
While their previous rehoming plea was rejected by France’s ministry of ecology earlier this year, the group has re-upped the bid to move them to said sanctuary, which they claim will give them more space to roam than the usual pool.
4
Twelve dolphins are also stranded at the park.
TideBreakers / SWNS
The team reportedly has experts from a whale sanctuary that was designed to house Keiko — the orca who starred in the 1993 family movie “Free Willy.”
See Also
Over 150 whales stranded on Australian beach cry out as rough seas hinder rescue efforts: ‘They are suffering’
“If you don’t even have a site, you’re years away from being a viable sanctuary,” said Marino, arguing why the Nova Scotia location might be the only viable choice. “We have a whole crew who know how to build and run a sanctuary.”
She added, “They have done it before, and I think we are the only team who has any experience in doing this.”
Time is reportedly running out for the stranded mammals.
Managers at Marineland, which is still legally responsible for the animals until they can be rehomed, stressed that Wikie and Keijo “must leave now” for their own welfare.
“Marineland reaffirms the extreme urgency of transferring the animals to an operational destination,” they declared.
Unfortunately, releasing Wikie and her son into the wild is not an option, as they were “both born in captivity” and therefore would likely not survive long, according to Schusterova.
“After entertaining the public for years, we should still provide them with a clean and safe environment to live out their remaining years,” she said.

44002032.article_content:
If you wanted to find an interesting Irish success story,
Stripe
co-founder
John Collison
would be up there with the best. One of the country’s youngest billionaires, the entrepreneur cofounded Stripe with his brother
Patrick
, and has transformed it into a global payments giant.
There are few people remaining in Stripe’s established markets that will not have used their services in one form or another, even if they don’t realise it. The company counts some of the biggest names in the world among its client list, from Ford and Hertz and Amazon to Zoom. At some point, customers have come into contact with Stripe’s technology.
Stripe has also captured a decent share of the
artificial intelligence
(AI) market, with OpenAI, Leonardo and Moonbeam among its customers.
Many of them attended Stripe Sessions in San Francisco, where this interview took place. The annual conference is the forum for Stripe to announce new products, float ideas and meet its customers in person.
READ MORE
Personal loans hit record as interest rates fall
EU may have to fund future drug development amid Trump moves
‘No long-term commitments to anything’ – the silent slowdown of Ireland’s economy
In 2019, a few years after the first Sessions was held, there were 1,000 people attending. This year, that had reached 8,000 attendees, up about 30 per cent on 2024. And Stripe plans to keep the event in San Francisco through 2028.
We meet at the halfway point of the event and Collison, the company’s president, is in a good mood.
“It has never felt busier in terms of a time in the industry with all the change we were talking about,” he says.
The previous day saw him take attendees through agentic AI, the next wave of the technology , before nudging Meta chief executive Mark Zuckerberg into revealing his true feelings on his fellow CEOs.
John Collison with Meta chief executive Mark Zuckerberg
The Collison brothers first hit the headlines in 2008 when their start-up Auctomatic was bought by Canadian company Live Current Media for a reported $5 million (€4.5 million). Not only did it fund their college education in the US – later put on hold as Stripe took off – but it also gave them a quick introduction to the start-up and acquisition process,  along with some valuable lessons.
From the start of Stripe, the brothers have said they are in it for the long haul. Fifteen years later, it remains a private company, despite breathless, almost annual speculation that this could be the year that Stripe finally goes public. In February, it emerged that the company was valued at $91.5 billion.
Stripe is dual headquartered in Dublin and the US, and employs around 8,500 globally.
When Stripe was set up in 2010, it had one aim in mind: to make it easier for developers to accept payments online. Fast forward to 2025 and it has significantly expanded its product range to include fraud prevention, invoices and billing, in-person payments and global payouts.
Customers can use the platform to create physical and virtual cards, or just accept payments without any code needed.
Last year at Sessions, the company announced it would no longer require customers to use its payments platform to access the rest of its services, essentially opening up tools such as billing and invoicing, fraud and risk verification, and in-person payments to companies that may not have been ready to shift everything over to Stripe just yet.
Businesses on Stripe are growing faster than the economy as a whole. The S&P 500 revenue growth is five-ish per cent. By comparison, the businesses on Stripe are growing in the 30s
The result, Collison says, has been positive. “It’s working pretty nicely. The particular thing we said was that oftentimes, for enterprises that have pretty complex stacks, if you ask them to change up everything at once – move their billing and their payments and so on – it makes it a really big job for them,” he says.
“It’s a way of making the Stripe functionality more adoptable piecemeal, which, especially with larger customers, makes it more practical for them. We’ve seen really good adoption of like payments and billing within the enterprise since then.”
Last year, the company hit $1.4 trillion in payments volume, continuing its growth trajectory. But although it is a large figure, it is still a small part of the whole payment ecosystem. That may change, with Collison noting the performance of companies using Stripe.
“Businesses on Stripe are growing faster than the economy as a whole. The S&P 500 revenue growth is five-ish per cent. By comparison, the businesses on Stripe are growing in the 30s. The reason for that is because we’ve lots of high-growth start-ups, and even for the large enterprises running on Stripe, like Fender, they were using it for the really high growth part of their businesses. And so that’s what drives it.”
This year, the focus was on two “gale force tailwinds” for growth:
cryptocurrency
, specifically stablecoins, and AI.

data.title: Show HN: A free AI risk assessment tool for LLM applications
data.author: percyding99
data.article_summary: 这篇文章简要介绍了如何使用GitHub账户登录TavoAI平台以访问AIRiskOps评估工具。用户需要同意服务条款和隐私政策才能继续登录。整个过程强调了使用已有GitHub账户进行登录的便捷性以及对相关条款的接受要求。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：该工具是否具备企业级安全性和合规性，是否适合在企业和严肃场合中使用。

不同观点：
• [hiatus的观点] 认为该工具需要通过如SOC 2或ISO 27001这样的审计，才能吸引大型企业用户。他指出，企业通常会期待有审计报告、渗透测试结果等安全保障，并在参与任何对话之前要求查看这些信息。

• [Cynddl的观点] 对该工具的GDPR合规性表示怀疑，指出其宣传中混用了GDPR和PII（美国概念），这在合规性上存在问题。Cynddl强调，GDPR使用的是“个人数据”的概念，而不是PII，这不仅仅是用词差异，还涉及到隐私保护的有效性问题。

• [alickz的观点] 对工具的创意表示赞赏，但指出网站上的“隐私”链接无法使用。同时，alickz关心该工具是否会使用扫描的代码库进行训练或其他用途。

• [Urahandystar的观点] 认为该工具可能更适合针对个人开发者或编程爱好者，而非企业市场。他建议通过小额交易来吸引个人用户，而非专注于企业市场。

补充讨论：
• 关于工具合规性的争议焦点在于其是否真正符合GDPR的要求，Cynddl指出其在合规性宣传上的不准确可能导致对隐私保护的误解。
• 安全性和透明度是hiatus关注的重点，他期望看到更多关于安全措施和审计结果的公开信息。
• alickz提出了对隐私保护实际操作的关切，尤其是对代码库的使用方式存在疑问。
• Urahandystar提出了市场定位的不同策略，认为个人开发者市场可能比企业市场更适合该工具。

这些观点共同构成了对该工具在安全性、合规性和市场定位上的多角度讨论。

43972083.article_content: Archisuit consists of an edition of four leisure jogging suits made for specific architectural structures in Los Angeles. The suits include the negative space of the structures and allow a wearer to fit into, or onto, structures designed to deny them. The project points at architecture as an arm of the law, a form that uses the built environment to police and control raced, classed and gendered bodies. Archisuits suggest a wearer might resist by not only being present but being present comfortably, leisurely.

- 争议焦点：虽然评论本身没有直接对比或争议，但潜在的讨论点可能包括该设计是否真的与ArchiZoom作品有足够的相似性，以及“时尚”与“实用”能否在现代设计中真正实现平衡。

data.title: Material 3 Expressive: Better, Easier, Emotional UX
data.author: meetpateltech
data.article_summary: Google的Material 3 Expressive是经过最深入研究的设计系统更新，旨在通过情感驱动的用户体验（UX）提升设计。该更新源于2022年一项研究引发的讨论：为何Google应用看起来单调乏味？团队通过三年研究和多次设计迭代，结合眼动追踪、调查和实验等方法，探索出更具表现力的设计。研究显示，各年龄段用户普遍偏好能激发情感的设计，尤其是18-24岁的年轻用户，对M3 Expressive设计的美观性和使用意愿评价极高。表现力设计通过颜色、形状、动作等元素，不仅增强视觉吸引力，还提升产品的现代感和用户情感连接。新的设计系统在易用性和无障碍设计方面也超越了现有标准。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Material Design 3（M3）的“表达性”设计及其在用户界面（UI）中的实用性和美学争议

不同观点：
• eviks认为，M3在某些方面（如按钮大小和颜色对比）超过了现有标准，但这导致了空间浪费和界面使用困难。他指出，虽然首次使用时找到按钮的时间缩短了，但整体界面可用性下降，且缺乏用户自定义功能来修复这些问题。
• onli对M3持混合态度。他认为M3的某些设计原则（如对象分组、对比度提升、动画优化）有帮助，但其扁平设计和奇怪的颜色搭配并不理想，且设计系统缺乏一致性。
• arp242对M3的“表达性”设计持怀疑态度，认为其所谓的“激发情感”不过是简单的按钮突出显示，缺乏真正的创新。
• jiehong认为M3在三年内只是简单地放大了UI元素和增加了色彩，建议使用平台惯例和工具包，以避免重复学习。
• boobsbr和saubeidl都对M3的设计趋势表示不满，boobsbr甚至表达了对Win98风格的怀念，而saubeidl则认为Material Design在Material 1时达到了巅峰。
• martin_a和jakubmazanec对页面设计细节（如改变光标和颜色选择）表示反感。
• AJRF指出，虽然M3的设计在视觉上可能不理想，但其设计目标是提高可用性，这与iOS的一些设计问题形成对比。
• rkachowski认为M3的设计趋势像是追随2022年的双色调潮流。
• anentropic关注Material Web的状态，质疑其是否仅限于Android平台。
• hokkos提到页面加载速度和M3设计中内容空间减少的问题。
• the_third_wave和xiphias2都对M3的整体设计持强烈批评态度，前者称之为“噩梦般的界面”，后者则强调了对老年用户的不友好。

补充讨论：
• 颜色和对比度：多个评论提到M3的颜色搭配和对比度问题，认为其不够美观且不利于可用性。
• 用户自定义：eviks和jiehong都提到缺乏用户自定义选项，认为这影响了界面的灵活性和适应性。
• 设计一致性：onli和saubeidl提到M3设计系统缺乏一致性，认为这是一个重要问题。
• 年龄和可用性：xiphias2特别提到老年用户在使用M3设计时的困难，认为设计应更具包容性。
• 设计趋势：arp242、boobsbr和rkachowski对M3追随设计趋势表示不满，认为其缺乏真正的创新。

争议焦点：
• M3的“表达性”设计是否真正提升了界面可用性，还是仅仅追求视觉效果。
• 颜色搭配和对比度的选择是否合适，是否影响了用户的实际使用体验。
• 设计系统的一致性和用户自定义功能的缺失是否是重要问题。

43975352.article_content:
Better, Easier, Emotional UX
The research behind Google’s bold new direction for design
Material 3 Expressive
is the most researched update to Google’s design system, ever. Here, Material researchers share the data behind the designs and new insights into users’ preference for emotion-driven UX.
Material 3 Expressive was born out of research — not in the
41 shades of blue
kind of way, which delegated design decisions to data, but in a collaborative inquiry spanning research, design, and engineering. Back in 2022, our research intern was studying user sentiment toward Material Design in Google apps. After mentioning her initial findings to colleagues in a Munich beer hall, she sparked a team-wide design debate: Why did all these apps look so similar? So boring? Wasn’t there room to dial up the
feeling
?
Over the past three years, we’ve explored the implications of this conversation, iterating through dozens of rounds of design and research to find the next evolution of Material Design. Through 46 separate research studies with hundreds of designs, and more than 18,000 participants from around the world, we’ve fine tuned a system that’s both beautiful and highly usable. Material 3 Expressive principles are rooted in solid research and built on long-standing usability best practices. Designers can confidently apply these new components and principles knowing they’re building something easy to use and connect with.
What is expressive design?
Expressive design makes you feel something. It inspires emotion, communicates function, and helps users achieve their goals. Want to dive deeper? Check out the official
Material 3 Expressive guidelines
. The fundamental parts of expressive design are the use of color, shape, size, motion, and containment. These design aspects are also fundamental to what makes a product more usable by drawing attention to what matters in the interface: making key actions stand out and grouping like elements together.
Material 3 Expressive's bold use of shape and color creates delightful user experiences.
Researching Material 3 Expressive
As the design team created initial concepts and explored how a more expressive design ethos could work across Google products, we embarked on a series of research studies using a variety of methods, including:
Eye tracking: Analyzing where users focused their attention
Surveys and focus groups: Gauging emotional responses to different designs
Experiments: Gathering sentiment and preferences
Usability: Seeing how quickly participants could understand and use an interface
To build a solid foundation, we started with research on individual components. For example: We evaluated options for progress indicators, assessing which made waiting time feel faster while also looking like it belonged on a premium phone. We studied how big a button can be, seeking improvements in tap time without overwhelming other items on the screen. We also ran several studies on the new floating
toolbar
, optimizing for designs perceived as modern, clean, and energetic as well as noticeable and usable.  And we ensured that our designs were following accessibility requirements and best practices. In many cases, we chose to exceed existing standards for tap target size, color contrast, and other important aspects that can make interfaces easier to use. This research helped us create the building blocks and guidelines needed for this new evolution of Material Design.
People prefer expressive designs
When it comes to design, people really do prefer to feel something. We found that well-applied, expressive design is strongly preferred by people of all ages, with that preference being particularly strong — up to 87% — among 18-to-24-year-olds.
While there was a net-positive indication across all age groups, younger study participants had the most enthusiastic preference for M3 Expressive and rated the designs as high in “visual appeal” and “intention to use.”
But top-level preference can only tell us so much. We wanted to dive into the design aspects that led to this preference. At last year’s Google I/O, we introduced a
set of attributes
that the Material team uses to compare designs. Maybe you noticed that many of these were emotional words? “Playful,” “energetic,” “creative,” “friendly,” and “positive vibe” are some examples. As we’ve been developing Material 3 Expressive, our researchers have worked with designers to iteratively test new screen designs against these attributes, helping to optimize the designs for a desired emotional reaction. In addition, we’ve sought to ensure that designs created with this new system are seen as more modern and visually appealing.
M3 Expressive designs were overwhelmingly rated higher for attributes such as “energetic,” “emotive,” “positive vibe,” “creative,” “playful,” and “friendly.”
Expressive designs feel relevant
Expressive design isn’t just about making a product look good; it can elevate how users perceive the product itself. We saw this in act

data.title: Zinc Microcapacitors Are the Best of Both Worlds
data.author: Brajeshwar
data.article_summary: 研究人员开发了锌离子微型电容器，结合了电池和超级电容器的优点，适用于小型设备。这种锌微型电容器具备高能量密度和快速充放电的特点，有望在需要长寿命和小体积的电子设备中找到应用空间。相比传统电池，它更安全、环保，同时提供了更高的功率密度，填补了电池和超级电容器之间的技术空白。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同类型的能量存储技术及其在特定应用中的适用性，主要围绕传感器节点和能量采集应用展开。

不同观点：
• myself248认为锌基或其他高性能电池技术适合用于能量采集较慢、消耗间歇的传感器节点。这种情况下，不需要很大的能量容量，但需要良好的功率密度以支持突发传输，并且需要非常高的循环耐久性。

• westurner质疑为何选择锌，而非碳材料。他引用了关于碳纳米管纤维的研究，指出这些材料具有很高的能量存储能力（583 Wh/kg），尽管这是通过机械扭转实现的。他还提到石墨烯超级电容器通常比（微型）电容器具有较低的能量密度。

• dvh则对使用C0G型电容器提出疑问，暗示这种电容器可能已经具备足够的性能，无需转向其他材料或技术。

补充讨论：
• westurner引用的研究表明，碳基材料，尤其是纳米技术，可能在能量存储密度上具有显著优势。
• myself248的论点基于实际应用中的需求，如功率密度和循环耐久性，而不仅仅是能量密度。
• 争议的焦点在于不同材料和技术在特定应用中的实际优势，如锌 vs 碳材料，以及C0G电容器的适用性。
• 讨论中提到了多种技术选项，如超级电容器和机械能量存储方法，显示出对多种解决方案的开放态度。

data.title: BuyMeACoffee silently dropped support for many countries, and nobody cares
data.author: beeburrt
data.article_summary: BuyMeACoffee平台悄然更改支付方式，导致许多乌克兰创作者无法提现。此前，这些创作者通过Payoneer接收付款，但平台在未通知用户的情况下，取消了Payoneer，仅保留Stripe作为唯一支付方式，而Stripe在乌克兰不可用。此举影响了依赖该平台作为收入来源的众多乌克兰创作者，尽管他们的资金仍在账户中，却无法提现。平台缺乏透明沟通，未在任何公开渠道或 changelog 中提及此变更，且对受影响用户的回应敷衍。该变化对非Stripe支持国家的创作者造成了实质性障碍，引发了对平台责任和公平性的质疑。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：支付和金融系统在合规压力下的运作方式，以及其对不同地区用户的影响

不同观点：
• 一些人认为金融和支付系统越来越倾向于通过严格的合规要求和风险控制来执行法律监管功能，甚至不惜牺牲小账户的利益。这种做法可能导致对某些高风险地区或用户的全面封锁，即使他们并没有明确的不当行为（rwarfield, znanz）。
• 另一种观点指出，这些公司首要任务是合规而非盈利，因此往往会采取保守策略，避免与任何可能涉及风险的用户打交道。这导致开户流程冗长，甚至直接拒绝某些高风险地区用户（znanz, jimjambw）。
• 有用户质疑是否应责怪这些公司，认为市场力量决定了他们对资源分配的决策，特别是在利润与合规成本不成比例的情况下（rckt, Kiro）。
• 另一种意见批评这些公司没有清晰、透明地告知用户其政策变化，导致用户在不知情的情况下受到影响，并认为这是不负责任的行为（florbnit, KronisLV）。

补充讨论：
• 一些用户分享了个人经历，说明由于支付系统的限制，他们无法顺利接收资金，甚至因为域名问题而被拒绝服务（gadders, casenmgreen）。
• 有建议指出，内容创作者可以通过集中管理赞助和推荐链接来帮助用户支持他们（gsky）。
• 还有讨论涉及替代支付方式，如加密货币，尽管其具有高波动性，但在某些情况下提供了跨国支付的解决方案（KronisLV）。
• 最后，一些技术细节如3D安全认证的支持问题也被提及，反映了支付系统在用户体验和安全性之间的权衡（nottorp）。

争议焦点：
• 支付和金融公司是否应为政策变化对用户造成的影响负责，特别是当这些变化没有清晰、透明地传达给用户时（florbnit, KronisLV）。
• 在合规与用户体验之间的平衡问题上，是否应优先考虑市场力量和利润，还是应通过更人性化的措施来减轻用户不便（rwarfield, rckt, KronisLV）。

44002333.article_content:
Silent changes in payment methods on big creator funding platforms raise some unpleasant questions.
UPD Aug 13, 2024:
The kind-of-official reply from BuyMeACoffee, and
my response to it
.
UPD Aug 14, 2024:
A support email to one of the users gives BuyMeACoffee’s reasons, and also they
blocked me on X (Twitter)
.
What happened
Recently, many Ukrainian creators have reported problems with payouts from
BuyMeACoffee
, a creator funding/crowdfunding platform.
At first, the reported support answers were typical corporative “we are sorry that we don’t care,” citing “compliance” and “policy updates.”
В оригіналі, щоб вестерни читали які там є нікчеми
pic.twitter.com/JxoGgamYLq
— Karå ꑭ🇺🇦 (@BzickOff)
August 2, 2024
Those reports were widely shared, and our predominantly feeling was “shocked but not surprised”: it is not the first time when a big platform has decided that they are too busy to try to distinguish non-occupied parts of a large country with a 30+m population from occupied parts, and decided they don’t care. Just recently, for example, the Mercury payment system
just blacklisted the entirety of Ukraine
alongside Iran and North Korea.
But in a few days, it turned out (again, from support messages shared on Twitter) that BuyMeACoffee
just dropped support for Payoneer
(which works in Ukraine), leaving Stripe (which doesn’t) as the
only payout method
.

support page

Buy Me a Coffee supports payouts to creators in several countries, facilitated through our payment provider, Stripe.
According to the Internet Archive, in
February

page
that listed Stripe and Payoneer, while
May’s snapshot
already has only Stripe-related links.
So, the change
in the documentation
happened somewhere between February (that’s when I personally used it for the last time) and May: Internet Archive doesn’t provide other snapshots between those two dates.
So, at least the support’s private answers were aligned with the documentation.

I know for a fact that some Ukrainian creators were receiving payouts via Payoneer somewhere around ~1 month ago; I even saw a credible claim about last week! (I just sent mine, which trickled from a moderately popular blog, will see whether it will come through; it is funny if it will. But more importantly,
there was NO communication about the change
. You wouldn’t find anything on
their Twitter
or in the
public changelog
(screenshotted at 2024-08-08 11:05:30 GMT+0300—just in case something will magically appear there retroactively):
As you can see,
there is nothing about payout updates
after the
Nov’23 post
, which mentioned Payoneer and Wise as available options alongside Stripe.
I assure you that
there was no email communication to the creators either
.
How bad is this?
The difference is public lists of supported countries between
Payoneer
and
Stripe
are
95 (ninety-five)
countries and territories. I am not sure that all 95 of those don’t have working Stripe (say, maybe the Faroe Islands just listed on Payoneer separately while being actually served by Stripe via Danish banks?), but it seems to be
a lot
anyway.
I’d like to know what the experience of BMaC users from those countries is like. But what I know for sure is that in Ukraine, a lot of people use the platform as a source of income (sometimes even a primary one). My subscriptions, for example, include but are not limited to:
A singer-songwriter turned paramedic who uses BMaC donations to record her songs on short vacations between duties;
A writer and culturology scholar turned soldier who funds his studies about Ukrainian culture and history;
A girl whose two brothers have fallen on the frontlines, and she funds her absolutely unique book club to connect to people and share reading experience with them;
A small business owner from Kharkiv who uses a “build in public” approach for a small coffee shop (and recently got mobilized into Armed Forces);
…and so on.
None of them have BMaC as their primary income, and still, it is a sign of support from their peers and the possibility to continue doing what’s important to them.
There is no way for any of us to receive the money accumulated on BMaC
anymore. What looks like “technical” change for some American is realistically
prohibitive
for those not privileged enough to live in Stripe-supported countries. The money is still “there”, so probably no lawyer can say BMaC has “stolen them”—you just can’t neither r
44002333.article_summary: BuyMeACoffee平台悄然更改支付方式，导致许多乌克兰创作者无法提现。此前，这些创作者通过Payoneer接收付款，但平台在未通知用户的情况下，取消了Payoneer，仅保留Stripe作为唯一支付方式，而Stripe在乌克兰不可用。此举影响了依赖该平台作为收入来源的众多乌克兰创作者，尽管他们的资金仍在账户中，却无法提现。平台缺乏透明沟通，未在任何公开渠道或 changelog 中提及此变更，且对受影响用户的回应敷衍。该变化对非Stripe支持国家的创作者造成了实质性障碍，引发了对平台责任和公平性的质疑。
44002333.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：支付和金融系统在合规压力下的运作方式，以及其对不同地区用户的影响

不同观点：
• 一些人认为金融和支付系统越来越倾向于通过严格的合规要求和风险控制来执行法律监管功能，甚至不惜牺牲小账户的利益。这种做法可能导致对某些高风险地区或用户的全面封锁，即使他们并没有明确的不当行为（rwarfield, znanz）。
• 另一种观点指出，这些公司首要任务是合规而非盈利，因此往往会采取保守策略，避免与任何可能涉及风险的用户打交道。这导致开户流程冗长，甚至直接拒绝某些高风险地区用户（znanz, jimjambw）。
• 有用户质疑是否应责怪这些公司，认为市场力量决定了他们对资源分配的决策，特别是在利润与合规成本不成比例的情况下（rckt, Kiro）。
• 另一种意见批评这些公司没有清晰、透明地告知用户其政策变化，导致用户在不知情的情况下受到影响，并认为这是不负责任的行为（florbnit, KronisLV）。

补充讨论：
• 一些用户分享了个人经历，说明由于支付系统的限制，他们无法顺利接收资金，甚至因为域名问题而被拒绝服务（gadders, casenmgreen）。
• 有建议指出，内容创作者可以通过集中管理赞助和推荐链接来帮助用户支持他们（gsky）。
• 还有讨论涉及替代支付方式，如加密货币，尽管其具有高波动性，但在某些情况下提供了跨国支付的解决方案（KronisLV）。
• 最后，一些技术细节如3D安全认证的支持问题也被提及，反映了支付系统在用户体验和安全性之间的权衡（nottorp）。

争议焦点：
• 支付和金融公司是否应为政策变化对用户造成的影响负责，特别是当这些变化没有清晰、透明地传达给用户时（florbnit, KronisLV）。
• 在合规与用户体验之间的平衡问题上，是否应优先考虑市场力量和利润，还是应通过更人性化的措施来减轻用户不便（rwarfield, rckt, KronisLV）。

data.author: weinzierl

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Coinbase数据泄露事件的影响及原因分析

不同观点：
• [mafriese] 认为数据泄露是通过收买在菲律宾的外包员工实现的，这些员工薪水较低（<1000美元/月），因此相对小额的贿赂（如5000美元）就可能获得大量用户数据。泄露的信息包括姓名、地址、电话、电子邮件、部分社保号码、银行账户信息和身份证件图像等，这对威胁行为者来说非常有价值。该用户还预测，可能会像Vastaamo数据泄露事件一样，出现针对个人用户的勒索行为。

• [silisili] 指出，公司为修复数据泄露事件可能需要花费1.8亿到4亿美元，并认为这是过度追求低成本外包客户支持（CS）服务的结果。该用户建议公司应该雇佣本地支持人员，并支付高于行业标准的薪资，以减少外包带来的安全隐患。

• [asim] 关注泄露数据的范围，询问是否所有客户数据都受到了影响，并指出如果整个客户群体的数据都被泄露，情况将非常严重。

• [Flex247A] 对事件发生的时间表示遗憾，因为这正值Coinbase被纳入S&P500指数，可能对公司声誉和市场表现产生负面影响。

补充讨论：
• 数据泄露的具体途径及外包员工的角色被详细讨论，特别是低薪外包员工可能被收买的风险。
• 数据泄露对个体用户的潜在威胁，包括个人信息被用于勒索的可能性，以及类似历史事件（如Vastaamo数据泄露）的参考。
• 公司为修复数据泄露所需的高额费用及其对公司策略的反思，特别是外包策略的调整。
• 事件对Coinbase在资本市场上的影响，尤其是被纳入S&P500指数这一时间点的敏感性。

data.author: Tomte

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Perl语言在2025年的适用性及Perl 5与Raku的比较

不同观点：
• Jiehong认为Perl 5在2025年仍然 largely 适用，尤其因为Perl 5.32+版本在大多数环境中（Windows除外）是预安装的，使用广泛。这表明Perl 5在未来几年仍有较大的使用基础和延续性。
• 同时，Jiehong指出Raku对许多默认设置做了大量更改，表明Raku在语言设计上与Perl 5有显著不同。然而，Jiehong也提到很少人使用Raku，暗示Raku的社区和生态可能不如Perl 5广泛和成熟。

补充讨论：
• Perl 5的预安装优势：Perl 5.32+在多个操作系统中预安装，这可能使其在未来几年内依然保持一定的流行度，因为用户无需额外安装即可使用。
• Raku的接受度：尽管Raku对语言进行了许多改进，但由于使用者较少，可能反映了其在开发者社区中的接受度仍较低。
• Perl 5与Raku的关系：Jiehong implicitly提出了Perl 5与Raku之间的竞争关系，讨论了两者在默认设置和社区使用方面的差异。

争议焦点：Perl 5和Raku在未来开发中的地位和接受度，尤其是Raku是否能扩大其用户基础以与Perl 5竞争。

data.title: Detecting Malicious Unicode
data.author: TangerineDream
data.article_summary: 文章讲述了curl项目中，贡献者James Fuller通过提交一个拉取请求，将脚本中的URL里的ASCII字符替换为外观相同的Unicode字符，结果无人发现。这个事件揭示了代码审查和CI任务的漏洞，促使curl团队改进检测机制。他们实施了新的CI任务，扫描并验证git库中的UTF-8序列，防止恶意Unicode字符被引入。同时，文章提到其他代码托管服务有类似警告功能，并介绍了检测类似字符的工具。作者强调安全是一个持续的挑战，需要不断改进以应对未知的攻击。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：域名变更是否构成安全警示以及如何防御潜在攻击

不同观点：
• [graemep 的观点] 域名变更，尤其是涉及Unicode符号的变更，应该被视为一个危险信号（red flag）。他认为差异（diff）显示出这种变化本身就值得警惕，可能暗示潜在的安全威胁。

• [fsflover 的观点] Qubes OS通过在隔离的虚拟机中运行所有软件，并且默认不将Unicode符号传递给主机，能够有效防御此类攻击。他引用了Qubes OS的官方公告（链接）作为论据，说明该操作系统如何应对类似的安全问题。

补充讨论：
• [争议焦点] 域名中的Unicode符号是否必然构成安全风险。graemep认为这是一个危险信号，而fsflover则提出了一种具体的技术解决方案，暗示通过适当的系统配置可以降低这种风险。

• [技术细节] fsflover提到了Qubes OS的具体防御机制，即使用虚拟机隔离和限制Unicode符号传递，从而减轻潜在攻击的危害。

• [实际应用] fsflover提供的链接指向Qubes OS的更新日志，具体说明了该操作系统如何处理相关问题，为讨论提供了实际的技术背景和解决方案。

44002589.article_content:
In a recent educational trick, curl contributor James Fuller submitted a pull-request to the project in which he suggested a larger cleanup of a set of scripts.
In a later presentation, he could show us how not a single human reviewer in the team nor any CI job had spotted or remarked on one of the changes he included: he replaced an ASCII letter with a Unicode alternative in a URL.
This was an eye-opener to several of us and we decided we needed to up our game. We are the curl project. We can do better.
GitHub
The replacement symbol looked identical to the ASCII version so it was not possible to visually spot this, but the diff viewer knows there is a difference.
In this GitHub website screenshot below I reproduced a similar case. The right-side version has the Latin letter ‘g’ replaced with the
Armenian letter co
. They appear to be the same.
GitHub shows a diff. But what is actually the difference?
The diff viewer says there is a difference but as a human it isn’t possible to detect what it is. Is it a flaw? Does it matter? If done “correctly”, it would be done together with a
real
and expected fix.
The impact of changing one or more letters in a URL can of course be devastating depending on conditions.
When I flagged about this rather big omission to GitHub people, I got barely no responses at all and I get the feeling the impact of this flaw is not understood and acknowledged. Or perhaps they are all just too busy implementing the next AI feature we don’t want.
Warnings
When we discussed this problem on Mastodon earlier this week, Viktor Szakats provided me with an example screenshot of doing a similar stunt with Gitea which quite helpfully highlights that there is something special about the replacement:
Gitea warns that the replacement is using “ambiguous Unicode characters”
I have been told that some of the other source code hosting services also show similar warnings.
As a user, I would actually like to know even more than this, but at least this warns about the proposed change clearly enough so that if this happens I would get the code manually and investigate before accepting such a change.
Detect
While we wait for GitHub to wake up and react (which I have no expectation will actually happen anytime soon), we have implemented checks to help us poor humans spot things like this.
To detect malicious Unicode.
We have added
a CI job
that scans all files and validates every UTF-8 sequence in the git repository.
In the curl git repository most files and most content are plain old ASCII so we can “easily” whitelist a small set of UTF-8 sequences and some specific files, the rest of the files are simply not allowed to use UTF-8 at all as they will then fail the CI job and turn up red.
In order to drive this change home, we went through all the test files in the curl repository and made sure that all the UTF-8 occurrences were instead replaced by other kind of escape sequences and similar. Some of them were also used more or less by mistake and could easily be replaced by their ASCII counterparts.
The next time someone tries this stunt on us it could be someone with less good intentions, but now ideally our CI will tell us.
Confusables
There are plenty of tools to find similar-looking characters in different Unicode sets. One of them is provided by the Unicode consortium themselves:
https://util.unicode.org/UnicodeJsps/confusables.jsp
Reactive
This was yet another security-related fix
reacting
on a demonstrated problem. I am sure there are plenty more problems which we have not yet thought about nor been shown and therefore we do not have adequate means to detect and act on automatically.
We want and strive to be proactive and tighten everything
before
malicious people exploit some weakness somewhere but security remains this never-ending race where we can only do the best we can and while
the other side
is working in silence and might at some future point attack us in new creative ways we had not anticipated.
That future unknown attack is a tricky thing.

data.title: Using TLA+ in the Real World to Understand a Glibc Bug (2020)
data.author: Tomte
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了作者使用TLA+形式化规范语言调查glibc中条件变量实现的一个 bug。TLA+ 通过运行程序的所有可能执行路径来验证断言的正确性，并在断言失败时提供最短的错误路径。这个 bug 表现为 `pthread_cond_signal()` 有时无法唤醒等待的线程，从而可能导致系统死锁。由于该问题涉及广泛使用的多线程机制，影响了许多编程语言和运行时环境。

作者详细说明了如何使用 TLA+ 来模拟和验证互斥锁、futex 和条件变量等并发原语，并通过具体代码示例展示了 TLA+ 的实现方式。虽然使用 TLA+ 分析复杂代码具有挑战性，但它提供了强大的工具来验证和尝试不同的修复方案，从而增强对代码正确性的信心。

总体而言，TLA+ 帮助验证和修复现实世界中的复杂 bug，展示了程序验证技术在处理大型和混乱代码方面的潜力。

Muscle Memory
muscle-mem
is a behavior cache for AI agents.
It is a Python SDK that records your agent's tool-calling patterns as it solves tasks, and will deterministically replay those learned trajectories whenever the task is encountered again, falling back to agent mode if edge cases are detected.
The goal of
muscle-mem
is to get LLMs out of the hotpath for repetitive tasks, increasing speed, reducing variability, and eliminating token costs for the many cases that
could have just been a script
.
It's unexplored territory, so all feedback is welcome!
Read
Muscle Mem - Removing LLM calls from Agents
for more context
Join
Muscle Mem discord
for feedback
Dev Log
May 7, 2025 -
First working demo
May 8, 2025 - Open sourced
How It Works
muscle-mem
is
not
another agent framework.
You implement your agent however you want, and then plug it into
muscle-mem
's engine.
When given a task, the engine will:
determine if the environment has been seen before (cache-hit), or if it's new (cache-miss) using
Checks
perform the task, either
using the retrieved trajectory on cache-hit,
or passing the task to your agent on cache-miss.
collect tool call events to add to cache as a new trajectory
It's all about Cache Validation
To add safe tool reuse to your agent, the critical question is cache validation. Ask yourself:
For each tool we give to our agent, what features in the environment can be used to indicate whether or not it's safe to perform that action?
If you can answer this, your agent can have Muscle Memory.
The API
Installation
pip install muscle-mem
Engine
The engine wraps your agent and serves as the primary executor of tasks.
It manages its own cache of previous trajectories, and determines when to invoke your agent.

@engine.tool
decorator instruments action-taking tools, so their invocations are recorded to the engine.

Each Check encapsulates:
A

data.article_summary: NASA's Stennis Space Center发布了首个开源软件——NASA数据采集系统同行评审工具。该工具旨在提升系统应用开发的协作效率，特别是支持火箭推进测试工作。由软件工程师Brandon Carver和Shane Cravens主导开发，该工具简化了代码评审过程，帮助开发者更早发现问题，提高软件质量和生产力。它专为与National Instruments的LabVIEW配合使用而设计，解决了图形化编程语言在代码对比上的挑战，提供了自动化和更有效的评审功能。通过将其开源，NASA希望全球开发者社区能进一步改进这一工具。

43971941.article_content:
4 min read
NASA Stennis Releases First Open-Source Software
NASA Stennis Communications
May 08, 2025
Article
Editor’s Note: The following is one of three related articles about the NASA Data Acquisition System and related efforts. Please visit
Stennis News – NASA
to access accompanying articles.
NASA software engineer Brandon Carver updates how the main data acquisition software processes information at NASA’s Stennis Space Center, where he has contributed to the creation of the center’s first-ever open-source software.
NASA/Danny Nowlin
Syncom Space Services software engineer Shane Cravens, the chief architect behind the first-ever open-source software at NASA’s Stennis Space Center, verifies operation of the site’s data acquisition hardware.
NASA/Danny Nowlin
NASA’s Stennis Space Center near Bay St. Louis, Mississippi, has released its first-ever open-source software, a peer review tool to facilitate more efficient and collaborative creation of systems applications, such as those used in its frontline government and commercial propulsion test work.
“Everyone knows NASA Stennis as the nation’s premier rocket propulsion test site,” said David Carver, acting chief of the Office of Test Data and Information Management. “We also are engaged in a range of key technology efforts. This latest open-source tool is an exciting example of that work, and one we anticipate will have a positive and widespread impact.”
The new NASA Data Acquisition System Peer Review Tool was developed over several years, built on lessons learned as site developers and engineers created software tools for use across the center’s sprawling test complex. It is designed to simplify and amplify the collaborative review process, allowing developers to build better and more effective software applications.
The new NASA Stennis Peer Review tool was developed using the same software processes that built NDAS. As center engineers and developers created software to monitor and analyze data from rocket propulsion tests, they collaborated with peers to optimize system efficiency. What began as an internal review process ultimately evolved into the open-source code now available to the public.
“We refined it (the peer review tool) over a period of time, and it has improved our process significantly,” said Brandon Carver (no relation), a NASA Stennis software engineer. “In early efforts, we were doing reviews manually, now our tool handles some of these steps for us. It has allowed us to focus more on reviewing key items in our software.”
Developers can improve time, efficiency, and address issues earlier when conducting software code reviews. The result is a better, more productive product.
The NASA Stennis tool is part of the larger NASA Data Acquisition System created at the center to help monitor and collect propulsion test data. It is designed to work with National Instruments LabVIEW, which is widely used by systems engineers and scientists to design applications. LabVIEW is unique in using graphics (visible icon objects) instead of a text-based programming language to create applications. The graphical approach makes it more challenging to compare codes in a review process.
“You cannot compare your code in the same way you do with a text-based language,” Brandon Carver said. “Our tool offers a process that allows developers to review these LabVIEW-developed programs and to focus more time on reviewing actual code updates.”
LabVIEW features a comparison tool, but NASA Stennis engineers identified ways they could improve the process, including by automating certain steps. The NASA Stennis tool makes it easier to post comments, pictures, and other elements in an online peer review to make discussions more effective.
The result is what NASA Stennis developers hope is a more streamlined, efficient process. “It really optimizes your time and provides everything you need to focus on right in front of you,” Brandon Carver said. “That’s why we wanted to open source this because when we were building the tool, we did not see anything like it, or we did not see anything that had features that we have.”
“By providing it to the open-source community, they can take our tool, find better ways of handling things, and refine it,” Brandon Carver said. “We want to allow those groups to modify it and become a community around the tool, so it is continuously improved. Ultimately, a peer review is to make stronger software or a stronger product and that is also true for this peer review tool.
“It is a good feeling to be part of the process and to see something created at the center now out in the larger world across the agency,” Brandon Carver said. “It is pretty exciting to be able to say that you can go get this software we have written and used,” he acknowledged. “NASA engineers have done this. I hope we continue to do it.”

AutoGenLib
The only library you'll need ever.
Import wisdom, export code.
AutoGenLib is a Python library that automatically generates code on-the-fly using OpenAI's API. When you try to import a module or function that doesn't exist, AutoGenLib creates it for you based on a high-level description of what you need.
Features
Dynamic Code Generation
: Import modules and functions that don't exist yet
Context-Aware
: New functions are generated with knowledge of existing code
Progressive Enhancement
: Add new functionality to existing modules seamlessly
No Default Caching
: Each import generates fresh code for more varied and creative results
Full Codebase Context
: LLM can see all previously generated modules for better consistency
Caller Code Analysis
: The LLM analyzes the actual code that's importing the module to better understand the context and requirements
Automatic Exception Handling
: All exceptions are sent to LLM to provide clear explanation and fixes for errors.
Installation
pip install autogenlib
Or install from source:
git clone https://github.com/cofob/autogenlib.git
cd
autogenlib
pip install -e
.
Requirements
Python 3.12+
OpenAI API key
Quick Start
Set OpenAI API key in
OPENAI_API_KEY
env variable.
# Import a function that doesn't exist yet - it will be automatically generated
from
autogenlib
.
tokens
import
generate_token
# Use the generated function
token
=
generate_token
(
length
=
32
)
print
(
token
)
How It Works
You initialize AutoGenLib with a description of what you need
When you import a module or function under the
autogenlib
namespace, the library:
Checks if the module/function already exists
If not, it analyzes the code that's performing the import to understand the context
It sends a request to OpenAI's API with your description and the context
The API generates the appropriate code
The code is validated and executed
The requested module/function becomes available for use
Examples
Generate a TOTP Generator
from
autogenlib
.
totp
import
totp_generator
print
(
totp_generator
(
"SECRETKEY123"
))
Add a Verification Function Later
# Later in your application, you need verification:
from
autogenlib
.
totp
import
verify_totp
result
=
verify_totp
(
"SECRETKEY123"
,
"123456"
)
print
(
f"Verification result:
{
result
}
"
)
Using Context-Awareness
# Import a function - AutoGenLib will see how your data is structured
from
autogenlib
.
processor
import
get_highest_score
# Define your data structure
data
=
[{
"user"
:
"Alice"
,
"score"
:
95
}, {
"user"
:
"Bob"
,
"score"
:
82
}]
# The function will work with your data structure without you having to specify details
print
(
get_highest_score
(
data
))
# Will correctly extract the highest score
Create Multiple Modules
# You can use init function to additionally hint the purpose of your library
from
autogenlib
import
init
init
(
"Cryptographic utility library"
)
# Generate encryption module
from
autogenlib
.
encryption
import
encrypt_text
,
decrypt_text
encrypted
=
encrypt_text
(
"Secret message"
,
"password123"
)
decrypted
=
decrypt_text
(
encrypted
,
"password123"
)
print
(
decrypted
)
# Generate hashing module
from
autogenlib
.
hashing
import
hash_password
,
verify_password
hashed
=
hash_password
(
"my_secure_password"
)
is_valid
=
verify_password
(
"my_secure_password"
,
hashed
)
print
(
f"Password valid:
{
is_valid
}
"
)
Configuration
Setting the OpenAI API Key
Set your OpenAI API key as an environment variable:
export
OPENAI_API_KEY=
"
your-api-key-here
"
#
Optional
export
OPENAI_API_BASE_URL=
"
https://openrouter.ai/api/v1
"
#
Use OpenRouter API
export
OPENAI_MODEL=
"
openai/gpt-4.1
"
Or in your Python code (not recommended for production):
import
os
os
.
environ
[
"OPENAI_API_KEY"
]
=
"your-api-key-here"
Caching Behavior
By default, AutoGenLib does not cache generated code. This means:
Each time you import a module, the LLM generates fresh code
You get more varied and often funnier results due to LLM hallucinations
The same import might produce different implementations across runs
If you want to enable caching (for consistency or to reduce API calls):
from
autogenlib
import
init
init
(
"Library for data processing"
,
enable_caching
=
True
)
Or toggle caching at runtime:
from
autogenlib
import
init
,
set_caching
init
(
"Library for data processing"
)
# Later in your code:
set_caching
(
True
)
# Enable

data.title: LLMs get lost in multi-turn conversation
data.author: simonpure
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了大语言模型（LLMs）在多轮对话中的表现，发现其性能显著低于单轮对话，平均下降39%。通过大规模模拟实验，作者分析了超过20万次对话，发现性能下降主要源于两个方面：能力的小幅损失和不可靠性的大幅增加。LLMs常在早期对话中做出假设并过早生成最终解决方案，导致出错后难以纠正。研究强调了LLMs在多轮对话中面临的挑战，即一旦走错方向，便容易迷失且无法恢复。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）工具中的对话管理和上下文处理问题

不同观点：
• Benjammer认为，保持对话上下文的“干净”至关重要，一旦上下文被“污染”，回复质量就会下降，且无法恢复，必须重新开始一个新对话。他还指出，对话只是产品界面的构造，实际上对LLM的回复质量有负面影响。

• Sharlin将LLM的这些问题归因于它们的过度自信和缺乏自我反思能力，特别是它们很少主动要求澄清问题，而是持续猜测用户的意图。他还质疑了用LLM替代人类程序员的可行性，因为与利益相关者的互动是编程中重要的一部分。

• Tmountain分享了一种有效的技术，即让LLM对当前对话进行简要总结，并将其用作新对话的起点，以避免携带多余的上下文负担。他预计这种技术很快会被自动化。

• Airylizard介绍了一种名为TSCE（Two-Step Contextual Enrichment）的框架，声称该方法在处理GPT-3.5和GPT-4.1的任务时显著提高了成功率，并提供了开源代码供他人测试。

• Zacksiri提出了一种双系统解决方案，其中一个系统是LLM本身，另一个系统动态管理上下文，帮助LLM将问题分解为小任务，并逐步聚合完成整个任务。

• Jumploops强调了在LLM工具中实现分支/分叉功能的必要性，以便更好地管理对话流程，特别是在编辑回复时不会丢失其他重要上下文。

• Podgorniy指出，单轮对话的接口设计存在问题，因为大多数用户期望线性对话。他分享了自己开发的Telegram机器人，通过“非回复消息意味着新对话”的方式解决上下文问题。

• T-kalinowski开发了promptdown工具，以便在每次对话历史时进行编辑，解决标准聊天接口不支持此功能的不足。

• Permo-w认为，当前的LLM领域中，人们在反复解决相同的问题，缺乏创新。

• Ranyume呼吁对LLM的上下文理解能力进行更多研究，并指出开发者需要明确知道如何有效利用这些工具，特别是在编码方面。

• Dr_dshiv推荐了一篇关于机器心理学的论文，认为其严谨且实用。

• Aleksituk分享了在数据处理任务中使用API和聊天窗口的经验，并探讨了如何将整个对话总结为一个可重复使用的提示。

• Zobat用幽默的方式将LLM比作瓶子里的精灵，认为它们在多次对话后会产生无意义的回复。

• Badmonster探讨了LLM在多轮对话中难以从早期错误中恢复的原因，可能是由于模型的训练数据、上下文窗口编码方式或架构瓶颈所致。

• Jsemrau基于游戏理论和代理推理的研究，认为需要良好的上下文管理以及任务执行前的规划过程，以确保模型的准确性。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中多次提到LLM在处理多轮对话时的局限性，尤其是当早期对话出现错误时，模型难以自我纠正。
• 一些用户分享了技术解决方案，如TSCE框架和promptdown工具，以改善LLM的对话管理。
• 争议的焦点在于LLM替代人类工作的可行性以及在实际应用中管理上下文和对话流的复杂性。

Title:
LLMs Get Lost In Multi-Turn Conversation
Authors:
Philippe Laban
,
Hiroaki Hayashi
,
Yingbo Zhou
,
Jennifer Neville
View a PDF of the paper titled LLMs Get Lost In Multi-Turn Conversation, by Philippe Laban and 3 other authors
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
Large Language Models (LLMs) are conversational interfaces. As such, LLMs have the potential to assist their users not only when they can fully specify the task at hand, but also to help them define, explore, and refine what they need through multi-turn conversational exchange. Although analysis of LLM conversation logs has confirmed that underspecification occurs frequently in user instructions, LLM evaluation has predominantly focused on the single-turn, fully-specified instruction setting. In this work, we perform large-scale simulation experiments to compare LLM performance in single- and multi-turn settings. Our experiments confirm that all the top open- and closed-weight LLMs we test exhibit significantly lower performance in multi-turn conversations than single-turn, with an average drop of 39% across six generation tasks. Analysis of 200,000+ simulated conversations decomposes the performance degradation into two components: a minor loss in aptitude and a significant increase in unreliability. We find that LLMs often make assumptions in early turns and prematurely attempt to generate final solutions, on which they overly rely. In simpler terms, we discover that *when LLMs take a wrong turn in a conversation, they get lost and do not recover*.

43991256.article_summary: 本文探讨了大语言模型（LLMs）在多轮对话中的表现，发现其性能显著低于单轮对话，平均下降39%。通过大规模模拟实验，作者分析了超过20万次对话，发现性能下降主要源于两个方面：能力的小幅损失和不可靠性的大幅增加。LLMs常在早期对话中做出假设并过早生成最终解决方案，导致出错后难以纠正。研究强调了LLMs在多轮对话中面临的挑战，即一旦走错方向，便容易迷失且无法恢复。
43991256.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）工具中的对话管理和上下文处理问题

不同观点：
• Benjammer认为，保持对话上下文的“干净”至关重要，一旦上下文被“污染”，回复质量就会下降，且无法恢复，必须重新开始一个新对话。他还指出，对话只是产品界面的构造，实际上对LLM的回复质量有负面影响。

• Sharlin将LLM的这些问题归因于它们的过度自信和缺乏自我反思能力，特别是它们很少主动要求澄清问题，而是持续猜测用户的意图。他还质疑了用LLM替代人类程序员的可行性，因为与利益相关者的互动是编程中重要的一部分。

• Tmountain分享了一种有效的技术，即让LLM对当前对话进行简要总结，并将其用作新对话的起点，以避免携带多余的上下文负担。他预计这种技术很快会被自动化。

• Airylizard介绍了一种名为TSCE（Two-Step Contextual Enrichment）的框架，声称该方法在处理GPT-3.5和GPT-4.1的任务时显著提高了成功率，并提供了开源代码供他人测试。

• Zacksiri提出了一种双系统解决方案，其中一个系统是LLM本身，另一个系统动态管理上下文，帮助LLM将问题分解为小任务，并逐步聚合完成整个任务。

• Jumploops强调了在LLM工具中实现分支/分叉功能的必要性，以便更好地管理对话流程，特别是在编辑回复时不会丢失其他重要上下文。

• Podgorniy指出，单轮对话的接口设计存在问题，因为大多数用户期望线性对话。他分享了自己开发的Telegram机器人，通过“非回复消息意味着新对话”的方式解决上下文问题。

• T-kalinowski开发了promptdown工具，以便在每次对话历史时进行编辑，解决标准聊天接口不支持此功能的不足。

• Permo-w认为，当前的LLM领域中，人们在反复解决相同的问题，缺乏创新。

• Ranyume呼吁对LLM的上下文理解能力进行更多研究，并指出开发者需要明确知道如何有效利用这些工具，特别是在编码方面。

• Dr_dshiv推荐了一篇关于机器心理学的论文，认为其严谨且实用。

• Aleksituk分享了在数据处理任务中使用API和聊天窗口的经验，并探讨了如何将整个对话总结为一个可重复使用的提示。

• Zobat用幽默的方式将LLM比作瓶子里的精灵，认为它们在多次对话后会产生无意义的回复。

• Badmonster探讨了LLM在多轮对话中难以从早期错误中恢复的原因，可能是由于模型的训练数据、上下文窗口编码方式或架构瓶颈所致。

• Jsemrau基于游戏理论和代理推理的研究，认为需要良好的上下文管理以及任务执行前的规划过程，以确保模型的准确性。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中多次提到LLM在处理多轮对话时的局限性，尤其是当早期对话出现错误时，模型难以自我纠正。
• 一些用户分享了技术解决方案，如TSCE框架和promptdown工具，以改善LLM的对话管理。
• 争议的焦点在于LLM替代人类工作的可行性以及在实际应用中管理上下文和对话流的复杂性。

data.author: stefankuehnel
data.article_summary:
**git-bug** 是一个去中心化、离线优先的 bug 追踪工具，嵌入在 Git 仓库中，通过 Git 对象管理问题、用户和评论，而非依赖文件。其主要特点包括：

1. **原生 Git 存储**：所有数据直接存储在 Git 中，保持版本控制和仓库整洁。
2. **分布式与版本化**：支持离线工作，并能无缝同步。
3. **快速**：问题列表和搜索可在毫秒内完成。
4. **第三方桥接**：支持与 GitHub、GitLab 等平台同步。
5. **多接口支持**：可通过命令行、终端 UI 或网页浏览器操作。
6. **易于集成**：安装和配置简单，快速上手。

项目采用 GPL-3.0 许可证，由社区贡献者开发和维护。用户可通过贡献代码或资助支持项目发展。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Git项目中的去中心化Bug跟踪工具及其使用和整合

不同观点：
• **赞赏去中心化Bug跟踪工具的观点**：
  - 用户`AceJohnny2`指出，使用Git的DAG（有向无环图）模型和不同的命名空间（如`refs/bugs/`、`refs/notes/`等）来存储数据非常有趣。他提到了Gerrit等其他项目如何利用不同的命名空间。
  - 用户`WD-42`表示支持本地优先软件的回归，认为GitHub越来越难用，尤其是在快速连接下。
  - 用户`rzwitserloot`长期以来一直呼吁构建基于Git的工单系统，认为该项目非常令人兴奋。

• **对整合和使用的疑虑**：
  - 用户`hungryhobbit`认为，虽然工具整合对工程师有帮助，但Bug跟踪器在很多公司还被支持团队、设计人员、QA团队和管理人员广泛使用。如果需要通过“桥接”来展示跟踪器，可能会导致额外的工序，并且效果可能不如专门设计的全功能跟踪器。

• **对平台依赖和集成的批评**：
  - 用户`ericfrederich`强烈反对GitHub、GitLab等平台将问题、合并请求等数据存储在中心化的关系数据库中。他希望问题、MRs、评论等数据能够随着Git仓库的去中心化一同分发，而不是依赖于某个特定的平台。

• **对许可证兼容性的关注**：
  - 用户`tiffanyh`提到，Git-bug选择了GPL3许可证，而Git本身是GPL2，这两个许可证是不兼容的，这可能带来问题。

• **技术细节和实现问题**：
  - 用户`badmonster`对多个用户在不同远程上同时修改同一问题或线程时的冲突解决机制表示关注，询问是否仅依赖Git的合并机制，还是应用了特定领域的启发式方法。

补充讨论：
• **工具对比**：
  - 用户`dannymi`提到`git-issue`是一个依赖更少的替代方案。
  - 用户`jhspt`提到自己的类似项目`git-task`，并谦虚地称其为“小小的项目”。

• **视觉展示**：
  - 用户`alasr`分享了Git-bug的截图链接，包括TUI录制和Web界面。
  - 用户`layer8`请求提供更多截图，并分享了2018年的TUI截图。

• **平台整合的可能性**：
  - 用户`silverliver`建议将此工具整合到如Forgejo或GitLab等开源SCM平台，而不是依赖于像GitHub这样的厂商锁定平台。

争议的焦点：
- 主要集中在去中心化Bug跟踪工具是否能够取代传统中心化平台的全功能跟踪系统，特别是在多团队、多角色使用场景下的适用性。

data.title: The Problem with Teens Isn't Smartphones–It's Their Families
data.author: illinx
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：文章关于 parenting 和技术（尤其是智能手机）对青少年心理健康影响的论证方法和结论的合理性。

不同观点：
• [lolinder] 认为文章的方法论存在严重缺陷，文章随意抛弃了许多研究，只依赖一个支持其结论的研究，并草率地认为技术不值得讨论。尽管 parenting 可能对孩子影响最大，但这不意味着技术的影响可以被完全忽视。教育领域中的边际收益研究也是有价值的。
  
• [wintermutestwin] 分享了历史上的类似现象，1988年加州的平等心理健康法实施后，许多 dysfunctional 家庭将孩子送入康复中心以逃避家庭责任。如今，社交媒体成为了新的指责对象，但问题根源仍在家庭。文章过于简化了问题，忽视了家庭环境的影响。

• [arp242] 指出文章可能陷入了 McNamara 谬误，即只关注可量化的自杀数据而忽略其他心理健康问题。仅凭单一研究就得出结论是不严谨的。

• [NikolaNovak] 不同意仅用自杀数据来验证心理健康危机，指出可能存在其他严重的心理健康问题但没有导致自杀。文章在数据选择上显得武断。

• [haswell] 认为文章过于简化地将问题归咎于手机，而忽视了社会接触减少和毒性话语的传播对家庭环境的影响。单用自杀率作为心理健康的代理指标是有问题的。

• [_rpxpx] 强调自杀率不能全面反映心理健康问题，自杀往往与机会和手段有关。文章傲慢地忽视了其他数据，且未听取青少年的意见。

• [ayushrodrigues] 认为自杀率不是衡量智能手机对青少年影响的合适指标，智能手机对注意力和动机的损害以及引发的ADHD问题更值得关注。

• [danielvf] 认为文章未能证明手机不是问题，且自杀数据的上升（尤其是女孩）本身就表明存在问题，文章更像是在制造争议而非提供有力论证。

• [nateburke] 对文章的数据呈现方式提出质疑，包括数据年份的选择和图表信息的混淆。

• [robg] 分享了学校数据，指出青少年睡眠不足与科技使用有关，且睡眠不足与心理健康问题相关。科技在家庭中的使用管理不如以往严格。

• [xlii] 认为欧洲与美国的比较不具可比性，因数据收集方式不同。问题的根源是多方面的，包括家庭经济压力和企业对注意力的剥削。

• [alistairSH] 认为问题本质上一直是心理健康护理的缺乏，而不是特定的科技或文化现象。

• [ndileas] 认为文章的观察虽然直观，但不一定准确，社会科学工具尚不足以解决如此复杂的问题。

• [huem0n] 认为文章忽略了诸如手机使用与霸凌率上升之间的证据，单一研究不能完全否定手机对青少年的负面影响。

• [codeduck] 认为自杀率不能单独作为心理健康问题的信号，社交媒体和手机在霸凌中的作用以及早期手机使用与不良后果的联系更应被重视。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于文章是否合理地论证了 parenting 是影响青少年心理健康的最主要因素，以及技术（尤其是手机）对青少年的实际影响。
- 许多评论者认为文章在数据选择和论证上存在缺陷，过于依赖单一研究和自杀率数据，而忽视了其他心理健康问题和复杂的社会因素。
- 家庭环境、社会经济压力、科技对注意力和社会互动的影响等也被认为是影响青少年心理健康的重要因素。

data.title: The average workday increased during the pandemic’s early weeks (2020)
data.author: robtherobber
data.article_summary: 一项由哈佛商学院Raffaella Sadun和Jeffrey Polzer等人进行的研究分析了300万人的工作模式，发现疫情期间远程办公导致工作日平均延长8.2%（约48.5分钟），员工参加的会议数量增加13%，但每次会议时间缩短20%。邮件数量也增加了5.2%，且有更多邮件在工作时间外发送。研究显示，远程工作模糊了生活与工作的界限，导致工作时间更长、更碎片化，员工感到疲惫。尽管会议时间缩短，视频会议的持续专注要求也让员工感到压力。研究还指出，较大的居家空间可能提升远程办公体验，而狭小空间则可能带来不便。总体而言，远程工作对员工的效率和情绪产生了复杂影响。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：远程工作时代的工作时长和生产力之间的关系

不同观点：
• PaulRobinson认为，每天工作4-5小时后，人们的生产力会下降。他指出，用发送电子邮件的数量来衡量生产力是有问题的，因为他在精疲力竭时也会发送电子邮件。他主张缩短工作时间以提高生产力，并建议进行A/B测试以验证这一观点。
• Koshima指出，远程工作节省了通勤时间，但工作时长却增加了，这是一个矛盾的现象。这种变化的原因可能是日历变得更易访问，或者管理者出于“眼不见，心不念”的恐惧增加了工作量。
• tmckd认为，疫情期间增加的工作时间对某些人来说是有益的，因为他们用节省下来的通勤时间进行远程工作，从而感到更快乐。尽管这只是个人经验，但这种模式在他认识的人中很常见。
• blitzar批评会议文化的失控，认为虽然工作时间增加，但实际有效的工作却减少了，很多会议纯粹是浪费时间。
• kleiba提到欧盟的公司必须遵守工时追踪法律，以防止员工无偿加班。他引用了一项分析，显示 pandemic 初期工作日平均增加了48.5分钟。
• bachmeier表示，疫情第一年他增加的工作时间大多花在了没有价值的任务上，如处理电子邮件和行政事务，这让他感到沮丧。

补充讨论：
• PeterStuer回顾了Java在早期被过度炒作的历史，并将其与后来.NET的崛起进行对比，但未直接涉及工作时长与生产力的讨论。
• nunez详细描述了远程工作中的会议负担，特别是对非晨型人的影响。他指出，在办公室环境中更容易进入工作状态，而在家工作则容易受到各种干扰。
• htk质疑是否需要调整面对面工作与远程工作之间的差异，因为面对面交流可能不需要那么多电子邮件和会议。
• SirMaster表示自己的工作时长和会议数量在疫情前后没有变化，认为个体差异可能很大。
• davio分享了一个公司通过禁止下午会议和设定会议时间KPI来减少会议时间的案例。
• bix6希望看到更长时间后的数据，以了解人们是否在适应后减少了工作时间。
• bluedino质疑平均工作时长的统计是否包括了那些在工作时间处理个人事务的人。
• sublinear强调应关注工作输出而非工作时间，认为管理者应关注工作质量而非工时，并指出将对话转移到文字或录音的改进效果。

争议焦点：
• 远程工作是否导致工作时间增加以及生产力下降。
• 电子邮件和会议是否是衡量生产力的有效指标。
